entries.content:
-- Example: a stepper. Up and down change the value. Left and right change the step. OK clears the value.
local function state(ctx)
  if not ctx.state.calc then
    ctx.state.calc = { value = 0, step = 1 }
  end
  return ctx.state.calc
end

function on_enter(ctx) ctx:invalidate() end

function on_input(ctx, ev)
  if ev.type ~= "key" or ev.state ~= "down" then return false end
  local s = state(ctx)
  if ev.key == "up" then s.value = s.value + s.step
  elseif ev.key == "down" then s.value = s.value - s.step
  elseif ev.key == "left" then s.step = math.max(1, math.floor(s.step / 10))
  elseif ev.key == "right" then s.step = math.min(1000, s.step * 10)
  elseif ev.key == "ok" then s.value = 0
  else return false end
  ctx:invalidate()
  return true
end

function on_draw(ctx, g)
  local s = state(ctx)
  local w, h = ctx.screen.width, ctx.screen.height
  local margin = math.max(24, math.floor(w * 0.06))
  local result_h = math.floor(h * 0.42)
  g:clear(0)
  g:rect(margin, margin, w - margin * 2, result_h, "fill", 15)
  g:text(margin + 20, margin + 28, "VALUE", { color = 0 })
  g:text(margin + 20, margin + math.floor(result_h * 0.45), tostring(s.value), { color = 0 })
  g:rect(margin, margin + result_h + 16, w - margin * 2, 72, "stroke", 15)
  g:text(margin + 20, margin + result_h + 40, "STEP " .. tostring(s.step), { color = 15 })
end

-- Example: read lines from a file declared in manifest.data_files. Progress stays in ctx.state.
local FILE = "items.tsv"

local function tr(ctx, key)
  if ctx.i18n and ctx.i18n.t then return ctx.i18n:t(key) end
  return key
end

function on_load(ctx)
  ctx.items = {}
  local reader = ctx.data:open_text(FILE)
  if not reader then return end
  reader:read_line()
  while true do
    local line = reader:read_line()
    if not line then break end
    local label, value = line:match("([^\t]+)\t([^\t]+)")
    if label then ctx.items[#ctx.items + 1] = { label = label, value = value } end
  end
  reader:close()
  if not ctx.state.index then ctx.state.index = 1 end
end

function on_enter(ctx) ctx:invalidate() end

function on_input(ctx, ev)
  if ev.type ~= "key" or ev.state ~= "down" or #ctx.items == 0 then return false end
  if ev.key == "down" or ev.key == "ok" then ctx.state.index = ctx.state.index % #ctx.items + 1
  elseif ev.key == "up" then ctx.state.index = (ctx.state.index - 2) % #ctx.items + 1
  else return false end
  ctx:invalidate()
  return true
end

function on_draw(ctx, g)
  g:clear(0)
  g:text(24, 24, tr(ctx, "title"), { color = 15 })
  local item = ctx.items[ctx.state.index or 1]
  if item then
    g:text(24, 90, item.label, { color = 15 })
    g:text(24, 130, item.value, { color = 15 })
  end
end

-- Example: the swap writes the final board immediately. on_tick only advances original, blank, and settled.
local PHASE_MS = { original = 400, blank = 500, settled = 400 }

local function state(ctx)
  if not ctx.state.grid then
    ctx.state.grid = {
      board = { 1, 1, 0, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0 },
      cursor = 3,
      animation = nil,
    }
  end
  return ctx.state.grid
end

local function clone(board)
  local copy = {}
  for index = 1, 9 do copy[index] = board[index] end
  return copy
end

local function full_row(board)
  for row = 0, 2 do
    local a = row * 3 + 1
    if board[a] == 1 and board[a + 1] == 1 and board[a + 2] == 1 then
      return { a, a + 1, a + 2 }
    end
  end
  return nil
end

local function adjacent(a, b)
  local ar, ac = math.floor((a - 1) / 3), (a - 1) % 3
  local br, bc = math.floor((b - 1) / 3), (b - 1) % 3
  return math.abs(ar - br) + math.abs(ac - bc) == 1
end

local function resolve_swap(board, a, b)
  if not adjacent(a, b) then return nil end
  local before = clone(board)
  before[a], before[b] = before[b], before[a]
  local cells = full_row(before)
  if not cells then return nil end
  local after = clone(before)
  for _, cell in ipairs(cells) do after[cell] = 0 end
  return { before = before, cells = cells, after = after, phase = "original", remaining = PHASE_MS.original }
end

function on_enter(ctx)
  ctx:set_tick_rate("normal")
  ctx:invalidate()
end

function on_tick(ctx, dt_ms)
  local s = state(ctx)
  local animation = s.animation
  if not animation then return end
  animation.remaining = animation.remaining - (dt_ms or 0)
  if animation.remaining > 0 then return end
  if animation.phase == "original" then
    animation.phase = "blank"
    animation.remaining = PHASE_MS.blank
  elseif animation.phase == "blank" then
    animation.phase = "settled"
    animation.remaining = PHASE_MS.settled
    s.board = animation.after
  else
    s.animation = nil
  end
  ctx:invalidate()
end

function on_input(ctx, ev)
  if ev.type ~= "key" or ev.state ~= "down" then return false end
  local s = state(ctx)
  if s.animation then return false end
  if ev.key == "left" then s.cursor = s.cursor - ((s.cursor - 1) % 3 == 0 and 0 or 1)
  elseif ev.key == "right" then s.cursor = s.cursor + ((s.cursor - 1) % 3 == 2 and 0 or 1)
  elseif ev.key == "up" then s.cursor = math.max(1, s.cursor - 3)
  elseif ev.key == "down" then s.cursor = math.min(9, s.cursor + 3)
  elseif ev.key == "ok" then
    local partner = s.cursor < 9 and s.cursor + 1 or s.cursor - 1
    s.animation = resolve_swap(s.board, s.cursor, partner)
    if not s.animation then return false end
  else return false end
  ctx:invalidate()
  return true
end

function on_draw(ctx, g)
  local s = state(ctx)
  local board = s.board
  local hidden = {}
  if s.animation and s.animation.phase == "blank" then
    board = s.animation.before
    for _, cell in ipairs(s.animation.cells) do hidden[cell] = true end
  elseif s.animation and s.animation.phase == "original" then
    board = s.animation.before
  end
  g:clear(0)
  g:text(24, 24, "SWAP WITH RIGHT", { color = 15 })
  local origin_x, origin_y, cell = 24, 70, 72
  for index = 1, 9 do
    local column = (index - 1) % 3
    local row = math.floor((index - 1) / 3)
    local x = origin_x + column * (cell + 8)
    local y = origin_y + row * (cell + 8)
    local selected = index == s.cursor
    g:rect(x, y, cell, cell, selected and "fill" or "stroke", 15)
    if not hidden[index] and board[index] == 1 then
      g:circle(x + 36, y + 36, 16, "fill", selected and 0 or 15)
    end
  end
end

-- Example: one rectangle function for drawing and hit testing. The focused card is inverted.
local LABELS = { "NOW", "NEXT", "LATER", "NOTES" }

local function state(ctx)
  ctx.state.cards = ctx.state.cards or { selected = 1, opened = 0 }
  return ctx.state.cards
end

local function layout(ctx)
  local w, h = ctx.screen.width, ctx.screen.height
  local margin = math.max(20, math.floor(w * 0.05))
  local gap = 12
  local card_w = math.floor((w - margin * 2 - gap) / 2)
  local card_h = math.floor((h - margin * 2 - gap) * 0.42)
  return { margin = margin, gap = gap, card_w = card_w, card_h = card_h, cards_y = margin + 36 }
end

local function card_position(l, index)
  local column = (index - 1) % 2
  local row = math.floor((index - 1) / 2)
  local x = l.margin + column * (l.card_w + l.gap)
  local y = l.cards_y + row * (l.card_h + l.gap)
  return x, y
end

local function hit_card(l, x, y)
  for index = 1, 4 do
    local left, top = card_position(l, index)
    if x >= left and x <= left + l.card_w and y >= top and y <= top + l.card_h then
      return index
    end
  end
  return nil
end

function on_enter(ctx) ctx:invalidate() end

function on_input(ctx, ev)
  local s = state(ctx)
  if ev.type == "key" and ev.state == "down" then
    if ev.key == "left" then s.selected = s.selected - ((s.selected - 1) % 2 == 0 and 0 or 1)
    elseif ev.key == "right" then s.selected = s.selected + ((s.selected - 1) % 2 == 1 and 0 or 1)
    elseif ev.key == "up" then s.selected = math.max(1, s.selected - 2)
    elseif ev.key == "down" then s.selected = math.min(4, s.selected + 2)
    elseif ev.key == "ok" then s.opened = s.selected
    else return false end
    ctx:invalidate()
    return true
  end
  if ev.type == "touch" and ev.gesture == "tap" then
    local index = hit_card(layout(ctx), ev.x or 0, ev.y or 0)
    if not index then return false end
    s.selected = index
    s.opened = index
    ctx:invalidate()
    return true
  end
  return false
end

function on_draw(ctx, g)
  local s = state(ctx)
  local l = layout(ctx)
  g:clear(0)
  g:text(l.margin, 24, s.opened > 0 and ("OPEN " .. LABELS[s.opened]) or "PICK A CARD", { color = 15 })
  for index = 1, 4 do
    local x, y = card_position(l, index)
    local selected = index == s.selected
    g:rect(x, y, l.card_w, l.card_h, selected and "fill" or "stroke", 15)
    g:text(x + 16, y + 28, LABELS[index], { color = selected and 0 or 15 })
  end
end

-- Example: seven-segment digits from g:rect, with a static panel on an offscreen layer.
local panel

local DIGIT_SEGMENTS = {
  ["0"] = "abcdef", ["1"] = "bc", ["2"] = "abdeg", ["3"] = "abcdg",
  ["4"] = "bcfg", ["5"] = "acdfg", ["6"] = "acdefg", ["7"] = "abc",
  ["8"] = "abcdefg", ["9"] = "abcdfg",
}

local function has_segment(segments, name)
  return segments and string.find(segments, name, 1, true) ~= nil
end

local function draw_digit(g, x, y, digit, scale, color)
  local segments = DIGIT_SEGMENTS[digit]
  local t, w, h = 8 * scale, 46 * scale, 80 * scale
  local half = math.floor(h / 2)
  local vertical_h = half - t
  if has_segment(segments, "a") then g:rect(x + t, y, w - t * 2, t, "fill", color) end
  if has_segment(segments, "b") then g:rect(x + w - t, y + t, t, vertical_h, "fill", color) end
  if has_segment(segments, "c") then g:rect(x + w - t, y + half, t, vertical_h, "fill", color) end
  if has_segment(segments, "d") then g:rect(x + t, y + h - t, w - t * 2, t, "fill", color) end
  if has_segment(segments, "e") then g:rect(x, y + half, t, vertical_h, "fill", color) end
  if has_segment(segments, "f") then g:rect(x, y + t, t, vertical_h, "fill", color) end
  if has_segment(segments, "g") then g:rect(x + t, y + half - math.floor(t / 2), w - t * 2, t, "fill", color) end
end

local function draw_colon(g, x, y, scale, color)
  local dot = 8 * scale
  g:rect(x, y + 20 * scale, dot, dot, "fill", color)
  g:rect(x, y + 52 * scale, dot, dot, "fill", color)
end

local function two_digits(value)
  if value < 10 then return "0" .. tostring(value) end
  return tostring(value)
end

function on_load(ctx)
  panel = ctx.layers:create(320, 160)
  panel:draw_with(function(g)
    g:rect(0, 0, 320, 160, "stroke", 15)
    g:line(20, 124, 300, 124, 15)
  end)
end

function on_enter(ctx)
  ctx:set_tick_rate("normal")
  ctx:invalidate()
end

function on_tick(ctx, dt_ms)
  local clock = ctx.sys:clock()
  local key = clock.valid and string.format("%02d%02d", clock.hour, clock.minute) or "unset"
  if key ~= ctx.state.shown_minute then
    ctx.state.shown_minute = key
    ctx:invalidate()
  end
end

function on_draw(ctx, g)
  local clock = ctx.sys:clock()
  local time = clock.valid and (two_digits(clock.hour) .. two_digits(clock.minute)) or "----"
  local scale, digit_w, gap, colon_w = 1, 46, 8, 18
  local time_w = digit_w * 4 + gap * 3 + colon_w
  local x = math.floor((ctx.screen.width - time_w) / 2)
  local y = math.floor((ctx.screen.height - 160) / 2)

  g:clear(0)
  g:layer(panel, math.floor((ctx.screen.width - 320) / 2), y - 40)
  draw_digit(g, x, y, string.sub(time, 1, 1), scale, 15)
  draw_digit(g, x + digit_w + gap, y, string.sub(time, 2, 2), scale, 15)
  draw_colon(g, x + digit_w * 2 + gap * 2, y, scale, 15)
  local right_x = x + digit_w * 2 + gap * 2 + colon_w
  draw_digit(g, right_x, y, string.sub(time, 3, 3), scale, 15)
  draw_digit(g, right_x + digit_w + gap, y, string.sub(time, 4, 4), scale, 15)
end

function on_unload(ctx)
  if panel then panel:dispose() end
end

-- Example: buttons are rebuilt from the current rule. The public view omits other seats' cards.
local function state(ctx)
  if not ctx.state.hand then
    ctx.state.hand = {
      mine = { 3, 9, 12 },
      remain = { 3, 5, 4 },
      target = 8,
      selected = 1,
    }
  end
  return ctx.state.hand
end

local function public_view(s)
  return { own = s.mine, remain = s.remain, target = s.target }
end

local function actions(s)
  local view = public_view(s)
  local card = view.own[s.selected]
  if not card or card <= view.target then
    return { { id = "pass", label = "PASS" } }
  end
  return {
    { id = "play", label = "PLAY" },
    { id = "pass", label = "PASS" },
  }
end

local function apply(s, id)
  local row = actions(s)
  local allowed = false
  for _, action in ipairs(row) do
    if action.id == id then allowed = true end
  end
  if not allowed then return end
  if id == "play" then
    table.remove(s.mine, s.selected)
    s.selected = math.max(1, math.min(s.selected, #s.mine))
    s.remain[1] = #s.mine
    s.target = 0
  end
end

function on_enter(ctx) ctx:invalidate() end

function on_input(ctx, ev)
  if ev.type ~= "key" or ev.state ~= "down" then return false end
  local s = state(ctx)
  local row = actions(s)
  if ev.key == "left" then s.selected = math.max(1, s.selected - 1)
  elseif ev.key == "right" then s.selected = math.min(#s.mine, s.selected + 1)
  elseif ev.key == "ok" then apply(s, row[1] and row[1].id or "pass")
  elseif ev.key == "back" and row[2] then apply(s, row[2].id)
  else return false end
  ctx:invalidate()
  return true
end

function on_draw(ctx, g)
  local s = state(ctx)
  local view = public_view(s)
  local w = ctx.screen.width
  g:clear(0)
  g:text(24, 28, "TARGET " .. tostring(view.target), { color = 15 })
  g:text(24, 64, "OTHERS " .. table.concat(view.remain, " "), { color = 15 })
  local x = 24
  for index, card in ipairs(view.own) do
    local selected = index == s.selected
    g:rect(x, 110, 64, 88, selected and "fill" or "stroke", 15)
    g:text(x + 18, 146, tostring(card), { color = selected and 0 or 15 })
    x = x + 76
  end
  local row = actions(s)
  local button_w = math.floor((w - 24 * 2 - 12 * (#row - 1)) / math.max(1, #row))
  for index, action in ipairs(row) do
    local left = 24 + (index - 1) * (button_w + 12)
    g:rect(left, 230, button_w, 56, index == 1 and "fill" or "stroke", 15)
    g:text(left + 16, 250, action.label, { color = index == 1 and 0 or 15 })
  end
end

-- Example: ctx.longtask:start, then ctx.longtask:feed on a wall-clock budget. Return without stop().
local BUDGET_MS = 2000
local FEED_EVERY_MS = 1000

local function state(ctx)
  ctx.state.search = ctx.state.search or { best = 0, done = false }
  return ctx.state.search
end

function on_enter(ctx)
  ctx:set_tick_rate("normal")
  ctx:invalidate()
end

function on_tick(ctx, _dt_ms)
  local s = state(ctx)
  if s.done then return end
  local started_ok, start_err = ctx.longtask:start()
  if started_ok ~= true then
    s.best = 0
    s.done = true
    s.err = tostring(start_err or "inactive")
    ctx:invalidate()
    return
  end
  local started = ctx.sys:millis() or 0
  local fed_at = started
  local best = 0
  for step = 1, 40 do
    local now = ctx.sys:millis() or started
    if now - started >= BUDGET_MS then break end
    best = step
    if now - fed_at >= FEED_EVERY_MS then
      local fed_ok, feed_err = ctx.longtask:feed()
      if fed_ok ~= true then
        error("watchdog feed failed: " .. tostring(feed_err or "inactive"), 0)
      end
      fed_at = now
    end
  end
  s.best = best
  s.done = true
  ctx:invalidate()
end

function on_draw(ctx, g)
  local s = state(ctx)
  g:clear(0)
  g:text(24, 48, s.done and ("BEST " .. tostring(s.best)) or "SEARCH", { color = 15 })
end

-- Example: start one GET, poll it from on_tick, and cancel it on leave.
-- The manifest must declare net.http. example.test is only a shape, not a live service.
local URL = "http://example.test/status"
local task_id

local function state(ctx)
  ctx.state.net = ctx.state.net or { status = "idle", body = "" }
  return ctx.state.net
end

function on_enter(ctx)
  local s = state(ctx)
  if s.status == "idle" and not task_id then
    local id, err = ctx.net:get(URL)
    if id then
      task_id = id
      s.status = "loading"
    else
      s.status = "error"
      s.body = tostring(err or "request failed")
    end
  end
  ctx:invalidate()
end

function on_tick(ctx, _dt_ms)
  if not task_id then return end
  local result = ctx.net:poll(task_id)
  if not result or not result.done then return end
  local s = state(ctx)
  task_id = nil
  if result.ok then
    s.status = "ready"
    s.body = tostring(result.body or "")
  else
    s.status = "error"
    s.body = tostring(result.err or result.status or "failed")
  end
  ctx:invalidate()
end

function on_leave(ctx)
  if task_id then ctx.net:cancel(task_id) end
  task_id = nil
end

function on_draw(ctx, g)
  local s = state(ctx)
  g:clear(0)
  g:text(24, 40, s.status, { color = 15 })
  if s.body ~= "" then g:text(24, 88, s.body, { color = 15 }) end
end

-- Example: list, read, and reveal are three values of screen.
local LINES = {
  "The river is wide.",
  "A lamp marks the pier.",
  "You can still turn back.",
}

local function state(ctx)
  ctx.state.pages = ctx.state.pages or { screen = "list", recite = 0 }
  return ctx.state.pages
end

function on_enter(ctx) ctx:invalidate() end

function on_input(ctx, ev)
  if ev.type ~= "key" or ev.state ~= "down" then return false end
  local s = state(ctx)
  if s.screen == "list" then
    if ev.key == "ok" then s.screen = "read"; s.recite = 0
    else return false end
  elseif s.screen == "read" then
    if ev.key == "ok" or ev.key == "down" then s.screen = "recite"; s.recite = 0
    elseif ev.key == "back" then s.screen = "list"
    else return false end
  else
    if ev.key == "ok" or ev.key == "down" then
      s.recite = math.min(#LINES, s.recite + 1)
    elseif ev.key == "up" then
      s.recite = math.max(0, s.recite - 1)
    elseif ev.key == "back" then
      s.screen = "read"
    else return false end
  end
  ctx:invalidate()
  return true
end

function on_draw(ctx, g)
  local s = state(ctx)
  local w = ctx.screen.width
  g:clear(0)
  if s.screen == "list" then
    g:text(24, 48, "ONE POEM", { color = 15 })
    g:text(24, 96, "OK TO OPEN", { color = 15 })
    return
  end
  g:text(24, 36, s.screen == "recite" and "REVEAL" or "READ", { color = 15 })
  for index, line in ipairs(LINES) do
    local y = 80 + (index - 1) * 48
    if s.screen == "recite" and index > s.recite then
      g:line(24, y + 16, math.min(w - 24, 24 + #line * 12), y + 16, 15)
    else
      g:text(24, y, line, { color = 15 })
    end
  end
end

-- Example: a counter stored in ctx.state. Up and down change it. OK resets it.
local function app_state(ctx)
  if not ctx.state.counter then ctx.state.counter = 0 end
  return ctx.state
end

function on_enter(ctx)
  ctx:invalidate()
end

function on_input(ctx, ev)
  if ev.type ~= "key" or ev.state ~= "down" then return false end
  local state = app_state(ctx)
  if ev.key == "up" then state.counter = state.counter + 1 end
  if ev.key == "down" then state.counter = math.max(0, state.counter - 1) end
  if ev.key == "ok" then state.counter = 0 end
  ctx:invalidate()
  return true
end

function on_draw(ctx, g)
  local state = app_state(ctx)
  local w, h = ctx.screen.width, ctx.screen.height
  local margin = math.max(24, math.floor(w * 0.06))
  g:clear(0)
  g:rect(margin, margin, w - margin * 2, math.floor(h * 0.55), "stroke", 15)
  g:text(margin + 20, margin + 28, "VALUE", { color = 15 })
  g:text(margin + 20, math.floor(h * 0.38), tostring(state.counter), { color = 15 })
  g:text(margin + 20, h - margin - 28, "UP +  DOWN -  OK RESET", { color = 15 })
end

-- Example: nodes and choices live in one table. Drawing and hit testing share choice rectangles.
local STORY = {
  start = {
    text = "A light is on at the end of the pier.",
    choices = {
      { label = "Walk closer", next = "pier" },
      { label = "Stay here", next = "stay" },
    },
  },
  pier = { text = "The lamp is warm. The path ends here.", choices = {} },
  stay = { text = "You wait. The light does not move.", choices = {} },
}

local function state(ctx)
  ctx.state.story = ctx.state.story or { node = "start", focus = 1 }
  return ctx.state.story
end

local function choice_rect(ctx, index, count)
  local w, h = ctx.screen.width, ctx.screen.height
  local margin = 24
  local slot_h = 64
  local y = h - margin - (count - index + 1) * slot_h
  return margin, y, w - margin * 2, slot_h - 8
end

local function hit_choice(ctx, count, x, y)
  for index = 1, count do
    local left, top, width, height = choice_rect(ctx, index, count)
    if x >= left and x <= left + width and y >= top and y <= top + height then
      return index
    end
  end
  return nil
end

local function choose(s, index)
  local node = STORY[s.node]
  local choice = node and node.choices and node.choices[index]
  if not choice then return false end
  s.node = choice.next
  s.focus = 1
  return true
end

function on_enter(ctx) ctx:invalidate() end

function on_input(ctx, ev)
  local s = state(ctx)
  local choices = (STORY[s.node] and STORY[s.node].choices) or {}
  if ev.type == "key" and ev.state == "down" then
    if ev.key == "up" then s.focus = math.max(1, s.focus - 1)
    elseif ev.key == "down" then s.focus = math.min(math.max(1, #choices), s.focus + 1)
    elseif ev.key == "ok" then
      if not choose(s, s.focus) then return false end
    else return false end
    ctx:invalidate()
    return true
  end
  if ev.type == "touch" and ev.gesture == "tap" then
    local index = hit_choice(ctx, #choices, ev.x or 0, ev.y or 0)
    if not index or not choose(s, index) then return false end
    ctx:invalidate()
    return true
  end
  return false
end

function on_draw(ctx, g)
  local s = state(ctx)
  local node = STORY[s.node]
  local choices = node.choices or {}
  g:clear(0)
  g:text(24, 48, node.text, { color = 15 })
  for index, choice in ipairs(choices) do
    local x, y, width, height = choice_rect(ctx, index, #choices)
    local selected = index == s.focus
    g:rect(x, y, width, height, selected and "fill" or "stroke", 15)
    g:text(x + 16, y + 22, choice.label, { color = selected and 0 or 15 })
  end
end

-- Example: one input starts a countdown across three poses. Session count and total stay in separate fields.
local RAISE_MS = 180
local HIT_MS = 220
local REST_MS = 200
local STRIKE_MS = RAISE_MS + HIT_MS + REST_MS

local function state(ctx)
  ctx.state.tap = ctx.state.tap or { session = 0, total = 0, goal = 8, strike_ms = 0 }
  return ctx.state.tap
end

local function pose(s)
  if s.strike_ms > HIT_MS + REST_MS then return "raise" end
  if s.strike_ms > REST_MS then return "hit" end
  return "rest"
end

local function strike(s)
  s.total = s.total + 1
  s.session = s.session + 1
  s.strike_ms = STRIKE_MS
  if s.session >= s.goal then
    s.session = 0
  end
end

function on_enter(ctx)
  ctx:set_tick_rate("high")
  ctx:invalidate()
end

function on_tick(ctx, dt_ms)
  local s = state(ctx)
  if s.strike_ms <= 0 then return end
  s.strike_ms = math.max(0, s.strike_ms - (dt_ms or 0))
  ctx:invalidate()
end

function on_input(ctx, ev)
  local s = state(ctx)
  if ev.type == "key" and ev.state == "down" then
    if ev.key == "ok" then strike(s)
    elseif ev.key == "up" then s.goal = math.min(36, s.goal + 4)
    elseif ev.key == "down" then s.goal = math.max(4, s.goal - 4)
    elseif ev.key == "back" then s.session = 0
    else return false end
    ctx:invalidate()
    return true
  end
  if ev.type == "touch" and ev.gesture == "tap" then
    strike(s)
    ctx:invalidate()
    return true
  end
  return false
end

function on_draw(ctx, g)
  local s = state(ctx)
  local w, h = ctx.screen.width, ctx.screen.height
  local cx, cy = math.floor(w / 2), math.floor(h * 0.46)
  local which = pose(s)
  local bob = which == "raise" and -36 or (which == "hit" and 18 or 0)
  g:clear(0)
  g:circle(cx, cy, 70, "stroke", 15)
  g:rect(cx - 10, cy - 110 + bob, 20, 70, "fill", 15)
  g:circle(cx, cy - 120 + bob, 16, "fill", 15)
  g:text(24, 28, "ROUND " .. tostring(s.session) .. "/" .. tostring(s.goal), { color = 15 })
  g:text(24, h - 48, "TOTAL " .. tostring(s.total), { color = 15 })
end

# 0. General rules, an example, and Manifest

This directory is the author contract for API 2.x. The current minor version is 2.11. `manifest.json` sets `"api": "2.0"`, `"2.1"`, `"2.2"`, `"2.3"`, `"2.4"`, `"2.5"`, `"2.6"`, `"2.7"`, `"2.8"`, `"2.9"`, `"2.10"`, or `"2.11"`. Anything marked 2.1, 2.2, 2.3, 2.4, 2.5, 2.6, 2.7, 2.8, 2.9, 2.10, or 2.11 exists only on a host that implements that minor version; see section 19. The text is split into sections `00`–`29` and appendices A–C. “This document” means the whole set.

1. Every call you write has a determined result. An optional capability is either present as a function or is nil (section 17).
2. One name does one thing. One operation has one spelling.
3. A parameter of the wrong type (a number where a table is required, nil where a string is required) raises a Lua error. The right type with a value outside the stated range returns `nil, "invalid_argument"`. Device, file, quota, and network failures return `nil, err`.
4. Predicates (`exists`, `is_*`) return only a boolean. A successful command returns nothing. A successful write or release returns true. A query returns the value it looked up.
5. Everything except the optional capabilities listed in section 17 is required of the host.
6. Every rule has a conformance test (section 20). A host is judged by those tests.

Error codes are a closed set. See section 18.

## Numeric parameters

A parameter described as an integer accepts an integer directly. A float that is exactly an integer (for example `240.0` from `w / 2`) is accepted as that integer. Any other float, NaN, or infinity returns `nil, "invalid_argument"`.

Coordinates and sizes are in `-32768..32767`, unless a narrower range is stated there. Drawing past the canvas is clipped. That is not an error.

A color is an integer `0..15`, an amount of ink: `0` is paper (white), `15` is the darkest ink (black).

An options table may be omitted. Omitting it is the same as an empty table. Fields the call does not recognize are ignored.

## A complete example

```lua
local F, count

function on_load(ctx)
  F = ctx.fonts
  local saved = ctx.storage:read("state.json")
  count = saved and ctx.json:decode(saved).count or 0
end

function on_draw(ctx, g)
  local w = ctx.screen.width
  g:clear()
  g:text(w // 2, 40, ctx.i18n:t("title"), { font = F.large, align = "center" })
  g:rect(40, 120, w - 80, 80, { radius = 12 })
  g:text(w // 2, 160, tostring(count), { align = "center", valign = "middle" })
end

function on_input(ctx, ev)
  if ev.type == "pointer" and ev.gesture == "tap"
     or ev.type == "key" and ev.key == "down" and ev.phase == "down" then
    count = count + 1
    ctx:invalidate()
    return true
  end
  return false            -- including back: hand control back; (2.7) the app exits after the user confirms
end

function on_leave(ctx)
  ctx.storage:write("state.json", ctx.json:encode({ count = count }))
end
```

## Manifest

| Field | Rule |
| --- | --- |
| `api` | `"2.<minor>"`. A minor newer than the host supports is refused at install. See section 19 |
| `app_id` | Application id. 1–63 bytes, character set `[a-z0-9._-]`. Required |
| `display_name` | Display name. A non-empty string. Required |
| `display_names` | 2.5: display names per language. An object whose keys are the `locale` values of section 8 and whose values are non-empty strings. Optional. The host uses the first one present of `display_names[locale]`, `display_names.zh` (for `zh-TW`), `display_names.en` (for languages other than `zh` and `zh-TW`), and `display_name`; when the system language changes, the next app list follows. The packager refuses unknown keys and empty values; the host ignores them |
| `version` | The application's own version string. Required |
| `author` `description` | Strings. May be omitted |
| `app_icon_s` `app_icon_l` `splash` | Packaged image keys. May be omitted. Suggested sizes are in appendix A |
| `entry` | Main script. Defaults to `index.lua` |
| `display.orientation` | `system`, `portrait`, or `landscape`. Defaults to `system` |
| `requires` | Array of strings, listed below. If the device fails any item, the app does not open (open reports `not_supported`; a host that can tell at install time refuses the install) |
| `permissions` | Array of strings: `net` (section 14), `reader` (2.1, section 22). An unknown name is refused at install |
| `preload_assets` | Array of image keys. A key not in the package is refused at install. Decoded before `on_load`; one failure does not block startup, and `ctx.package:image` tries again |
| `data_files` | Data files `ctx.package` may read. An array of `{ name, format, max_bytes }`: `format` is `txt`, `tsv`, or `json`, the extension of `name` matches it, the file lives under the package `data/`, and it does not exceed `max_bytes`. Otherwise both packaging and install fail |
| `ttf_reserve_kb` | Integer 512–4096. Memory for TTF is reserved at the start of the session: either this field is set, or `requires` contains `ttf` (then the default is 2048). Otherwise this session has no TTF (section 7) |
| `lockscreen.entry` | Lock-screen script. Required when a `lockscreen` object is present. A script missing from the package is refused at install |
| `lockscreen.interval_sec` | Integer. Defaults to 60. Clamped to 30–3600 at install |

Names `requires` may use:

| Name | Requirement |
| --- | --- |
| `pointer` | The device has a touchscreen |
| `up` `down` `left` `right` `ok` | The device has this key built in (a Bluetooth peripheral does not count) |
| `pattern` `image_transform` `ttf` `ui` | Optional capabilities in section 17 |
| `reader` `dialog` `frontlight` `image_decode` | 2.1 optional capabilities in section 17 |
| `lockscreen_timer` | The device can wake on a timer to refresh the lock screen |

An unknown name is refused at install. Every device has `back`; do not list it. The core flow uses only the input `requires` guarantees, plus `back`.
entries.example:
local F, count

function on_load(ctx)
  F = ctx.fonts
  local saved = ctx.storage:read("state.json")
  count = saved and ctx.json:decode(saved).count or 0
end

function on_draw(ctx, g)
  local w = ctx.screen.width
  g:clear()
  g:text(w // 2, 40, ctx.i18n:t("title"), { font = F.large, align = "center" })
  g:rect(40, 120, w - 80, 80, { radius = 12 })
  g:text(w // 2, 160, tostring(count), { align = "center", valign = "middle" })
end

function on_input(ctx, ev)
  if ev.type == "pointer" and ev.gesture == "tap"
     or ev.type == "key" and ev.key == "down" and ev.phase == "down" then
    count = count + 1
    ctx:invalidate()
    return true
  end
  return false            -- including back: hand control back; (2.7) the app exits after the user confirms
end

function on_leave(ctx)
  ctx.storage:write("state.json", ctx.json:encode({ count = count }))
end

entries.content:
# 1. Language and the sandbox

Lua 5.5, with 32-bit numbers: integers are signed 32-bit integers, and floats are single precision (`float`). The device processor has only single-precision float hardware. 64-bit integers and double precision would be emulated in software, and that is much slower.

- `math.maxinteger` is `2147483647`. `math.mininteger` is `-2147483648`. Integer add, subtract, and multiply wrap in two's complement when they leave the range.
- Integer operations (`+ - * // %`, and bitwise operations) produce integers. `/` and `^` produce floats.
- Single precision has about 7 significant digits. The contiguous integers that are exact stop at `16777216`. Use integers and `//` for coordinates, counts, and amounts of money.

Open standard libraries: `base`, `table`, `string`, `math`, `utf8`, `coroutine`. `math.random` is seeded differently at the start of each session.

Not present as globals: `io`, `os`, `package`, `debug`, `dofile`, `loadfile`, `load`, `print`, `collectgarbage`. `getmetatable("")` returns false. String methods still work.

`require(name)` loads only a script from this package: replace `.` with `/` and append `.lua`. A module runs once per session, then the cached result is returned. A missing module, a name that contains `..`, or a name that starts with `/` raises the Lua error `module 'name' not found`.

## Memory

The script heap is at least 2 MB (not counting `ttf_reserve_kb`). The actual size depends on memory the device still has free. A failed allocation is a Lua error (`not enough memory`) and can be caught with `pcall`. Collection is `ctx.gc` in section 12.

## Errors

An error raised in a callback and not caught, or a callback that runs out of time, ends this session: no further callback runs (including `on_leave`). The host shows an error screen, then returns to the system. Files written before that are kept.

# 2. Lifecycle

A session starts at load and ends at leave. When the session ends the virtual machine is destroyed. The next open is a new session. State continues only through the files in section 9 and (2.2) `ctx.state` from section 28.

Load order: `on_load`, then the host draws the first frame (it calls `on_draw`). During load the screen keeps the picture from before the open; there is no splash image. When load takes longer than about 0.8 seconds, the host first shows the system opening page (this app's icon card and "Opening...", see appendix A, "Icons"). A lock-screen session (section 15) shows no opening page; the screen stays as it was before the lock. To show a picture sooner, do only what the first frame needs in `on_load` and move the rest to later callbacks.

A function that does not exist is skipped.

| Function | When | Limit |
| --- | --- | ---: |
| `on_load(ctx)` | The session is loaded | 2000 ms |
| `on_draw(ctx, g)` | A frame needs to be drawn. `g` is this frame's canvas (section 6) | 1500 ms |
| `on_input(ctx, ev)` | A key or a pointer (section 4). Return `true` to say it was handled | 1000 ms |
| `on_tick(ctx, dt_ms)` | Wakes on the `set_tick` period | 1000 ms |
| `on_pause(ctx)` | A system screen covers the app (text input, a dialog, (2.7) the exit confirmation, and so on) | 1000 ms |
| `on_resume(ctx)` | The cover goes away. The host then redraws one frame | 1000 ms |
| `on_leave(ctx)` | The last callback before the session ends | 1000 ms |

The timer function of `ctx:after`, the completion function of `ctx.net:request` and of `ctx.input:text`, (2.1) the completion function of `ctx.dialog`, (2.6) the WebSocket `on_open`, `on_message`, and `on_close`, and (2.9) the docked-input `on_change` and `on_end` are callbacks too. Their limit is 1000 ms.

While paused (from `on_pause` until `on_resume`) the host does not call `on_input`, `on_tick`, timer functions, completion functions, or (2.6) WebSocket callbacks. After `on_resume` returns, the host first redraws one frame, then calls the timer functions and completion functions that came due during the pause, and the queued WebSocket callbacks, in order.

Any callback may call the interfaces in this document (the canvas is valid only in `on_draw` and `layer:draw`), including starting a network request or setting a timer from `on_load`.

## Time budget

The limit is wall-clock time, measured from the start of the callback. The host checks between Lua instructions. A slow host function (decoding an image, opening a font, reading or writing a file) is not interrupted. The check happens at the next instruction after it returns. Running over the limit aborts that callback. The error text contains `time budget`. After `pcall` catches it, the host raises it again at the next instruction.

```lua
ctx.budget:extend()
```

Moves the deadline of the current callback to 11000 ms after the moment of the call, and returns true, but the deadline is no later than 30000 ms after the callback started. Called from `on_leave`, or outside a callback, it returns `nil, "inactive"`.

Lua on the device is much slower than on a computer. The following are reference values measured on the Gancao X4 Pro / X4 Classic (2026-10-16 firmware), not guarantees: one virtual machine instruction takes about 0.45 µs and newly allocated memory about 0.2 µs per byte, roughly a hundredth of the speed of a desktop browser; library calls such as `string.format` and string concatenation are just as slow. For JSON and private files see sections 10 and 9. A loop that takes a few milliseconds on a computer may take several hundred on the device. When the work in one callback gets close to its limit, split it over several timer callbacks.

## Tick and timers

```lua
ctx:set_tick(ms)
local timer = ctx:after(ms, function(ctx) end)
timer:cancel()
```

`set_tick` sets the period of `on_tick`. `ms` is an integer from 33 to 60000, or 0 to stop. At the start of the session it is 0, and `on_tick` is not called. The period is the target gap between the starts of two `on_tick` calls. If the previous callback has not finished, the next one waits. Missed ticks are not made up. `dt_ms` is the milliseconds since the previous `on_tick` (since `set_tick`, the first time).

Presenting one frame on an e-ink panel takes a few hundred milliseconds. Frames requested while a present is in progress are composed into one frame. The host may call `on_draw` for that frame while the previous one is still refreshing; it draws the state at that moment, and the frame is shown once the previous refresh finishes. The frame rate on the panel is therefore set by presenting: a partial refresh on the Gancao X4 Pro and X4 Classic takes about 650 ms per frame (about 75 ms to render, about 570 ms to refresh), under 1.5 frames per second, so the displacement between two adjacent frames is speed × 0.65 seconds. The frame on which the system inserts its automatic full refresh takes about 1.5 seconds (section 5). Whether `on_tick` keeps running during a present depends on the device: on the X4 Pro it is called on its period as usual; on the X4 Classic, once the next frame is taken, no callback runs until that frame is shown, so while frames are requested back to back there is one `on_tick` per frame and `dt_ms` is about 650. Gancao firmware before 2026-10-16 behaves the same way. Animate by time: advance continuous motion by speed × `dt_ms`. Do not move one fixed step per `on_tick` or `on_draw`, and do not cap `dt_ms` or a single displacement; otherwise the speed differs several times between devices. When the jump between two frames is too large to read as continuous, use a discrete motion by cell or by step, or draw only the start and the end.

The `set_tick` period is rounded to the device's system tick: Gancao firmware ticks every 10 ms, so `set_tick(33)` runs about every 40 ms.

`after` calls the function once after `ms` milliseconds. `ms` is an integer from 1 to 2147483647. At most 32 timers may be pending at once. The 33rd returns `nil, "limit_exceeded"`. It returns the timer object. `cancel` stops a pending timer from firing and returns nothing. It has no effect on a timer that has already fired or already been cancelled.

Waking only when needed saves power: align a clock face to the next minute with `ctx:after`, and use `set_tick` only for animation.

## How a session ends

Each of the following calls `on_leave` (unless the session has already ended because of an error), then destroys the virtual machine:

| Cause | When |
| --- | --- |
| The app leaves | The script calls `ctx:quit()`, after the current callback returns |
| A system page opens | The script calls `ctx.system:open` (2.1, section 25), after the current callback returns |
| Back was not handled | `on_input` for `back` did not return `true`; (2.7) after the user chooses to exit in the exit confirmation (section 4) |
| Forced exit | A long press of Back (section 4) |
| Back to Home | A system key goes to the home screen, for example a long press of the `x4_pro` Home key (section 4) |
| The lock screen starts | The system decides to lock (section 15) |
| Power off | The user powers off, or low battery powers off |

When `on_leave` starts, unfinished network exchanges, text input, (2.9) docked input, dialogs, and pending timers are cancelled. Their functions are not called. A file written in `on_leave` is flushed before the virtual machine is destroyed. Within 1000 ms at least 256 KB of writes can finish. (2.2) After `on_leave` returns, the host saves `ctx.state` (section 28); this does not count against the `on_leave` limit.

`ctx:quit()` returns nothing.

When a system screen covers the app and a finger is still down, the host delivers a pointer `cancel` first, then `on_pause`.

# 3. Screen and device

```lua
ctx.screen.width
ctx.screen.height
ctx.screen.orientation    -- "portrait" | "landscape"
ctx.screen.occlusion      -- { top, right, bottom, left }, pixels hidden by the bezel
ctx.screen.gray_levels    -- gray levels the app's drawing actually shows
ctx.screen.gray_still     -- 2.11: gray levels a gray frame shows, 4 or 2
ctx.device.model          -- device profile name, see the table below
ctx.device.lock_timer     -- whether a timer can wake the lock screen (the "timer wake" column), boolean
ctx.device.name           -- 2.1: the name the user gave the device
ctx.device.firmware       -- 2.1: firmware version string
ctx.device.id_for_app     -- 2.1: a device id that differs per app
```

`id_for_app` is 32 lowercase hex characters. On one device the same `app_id` always gets the same value. A different app gets a different value, and a different device gets a different value. Use it as an online account or a leaderboard identity. It is not the device serial number, and the serial number cannot be derived from it. Uninstalling and reinstalling does not change it.

Width greater than height is landscape. When `display.orientation` is `portrait` or `landscape`, these fields do not change during the session. When it is `system`, rotation happens only between callbacks: the next callback sees the new width, height, orientation, and `occlusion`, and a redraw is already scheduled. The origin is the top left of the logical screen, x increases to the right, y increases downward. Pointer coordinates are already converted for the rotation.

Pixels inside `occlusion` are drawn as usual. They are just not visible. Put text, strokes, focus, and hit targets in the visible area.

## Gray levels

The host maps a color onto `gray_levels` steps. The step is `(color * gray_levels) // 16`. Step 0 is the lightest.

An e-ink panel needs a dedicated grayscale waveform and a full refresh (the whole screen flashes) before it can show intermediate gray. An app frame uses the fast refresh, which is black and white only, so every current profile has `gray_levels` of 2. How many gray steps the panel itself can show is a separate fact.

- When `gray_levels` is 2, `0..7` is drawn as paper and `8..15` is drawn as ink. Use `g:pattern` for a middle tone (section 6).
- Antialiasing on the edge of TTF text may use more steps of the panel. This limit does not apply to that.

Body text and controls use `0` and `15`. The result is the same on every device.

### Gray frames (2.11)

A still picture (a photo album, a cover, a map) can show intermediate gray with the grayscale waveform. If any `g:image` call in a frame sets `gray = true` (section 6), that frame is a gray frame:

- The whole frame is drawn in `gray_still` steps. The step is `(color * gray_still) // 16`, the same for rectangles, lines, text, and images. A 4-level image keeps its own 4 levels, and a black-and-white image stays black and white.
- It is a full refresh with the grayscale waveform. The whole screen flashes once, slower than a normal full refresh, so it does not suit animation. The first normal frame after a gray frame is also a full refresh, to clear the intermediate gray.
- `gray_levels` does not change. It is still the number of steps of a normal frame.

On a device whose `gray_still` is 2, `gray` is ignored and the frame stays black and white. `gray` also has no effect, and the frame is drawn as usual, in these cases: inside a layer's `layer:draw` (layers are black and white, section 11), and in a lock-screen session (section 15). While a system input method, dialog, or similar covers the app's picture, the host turns that frame into a normal full refresh.

`gray_still` depends on the device and the panel. Check it; do not infer it from the device profile.

**4-level images in normal frames** (2.11): in a package whose manifest sets `"api": "2.11"` or later, a 4-level image (a 4-level image in the package, or an image `ctx.image:decode` decodes with `gray = true`, section 27) is drawn in a normal frame as a 4×4 dot pattern fixed to the canvas. The four steps 0, 5, 10, and 15 come out as about 0, 6/16, 11/16, and all ink dots, and the dots of neighboring images line up. A package of 2.10 or earlier is still drawn with the threshold above, and its picture does not change.

## Device profiles

| `model` | Portrait | Touch | Built-in keys | Gray levels | small / medium / large | Timer wake | Front light | Portrait occlusion top/right/bottom/left | Docked keyboard height (2.9) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `x4_pro` | 480×800 | yes | `up` `down` `back` | 2 | 20 / 24 / 30 | yes | yes, warmth is adjustable | 0 / 0 / 0 / 0 | 340 |
| `x4_classic` | 480×800 | no | `up` `down` `left` `right` `ok` `back` | 2 | 20 / 24 / 30 | yes | no | 0 / 0 / 0 / 0 | 0 |

A type size is the line height in pixels. A new profile may only add a row to this table, and the row must fill every column.

Every profile has a touchscreen, or it has `up`, `down`, and `ok` together, so the UI library in section 16 can be operated on every profile. The largest system font is 40 px. Larger type (clock digits and the like) uses TTF: (2.3) `ctx.fonts:size(px)` takes the preferred font directly, or choose one yourself with `installed` and `open` (section 7).

# 4. Input

```lua
ctx.input.keys      -- { up, down, left, right, ok, back }, each a boolean
ctx.input.pointer   -- true when there is a touchscreen
```

Both tables are written at the start of every callback. `back` is always true. A key built into the device is always true. While a Bluetooth page turner is connected, `up` and `down` are true, and its previous-page and next-page controls are delivered as `up` and `down`. (2.10) While a Bluetooth keyboard is connected, `up`, `down`, `left`, `right`, and `ok` are all true; see "Physical keyboard". A key that is false produces no events. The power key produces no events.

## Keys

```lua
{ type = "key", key = "ok", phase = "down", time_ms = 0 }
```

`phase` is `down` or `up`. One press is one pair. There is no auto-repeat (from 2.10, holding a key on a Bluetooth keyboard may deliver several pairs in a row, and a listening app also gets `repeat`; see "Physical keyboard"). `time_ms` is the same counter as `ctx.clock:millis()`.

## Back

- **Short press** (held for less than 1000 ms): on release the host delivers `down` and then `up` for `back`, back to back. Only the return value of the `up` event matters: if it is not `true`, the host shows an exit confirmation (below), and the app exits once the user confirms. The return value of the `down` event does nothing. Handle “go to the previous page” in `up`.
- **Long press** (held for 1000 ms): no event is delivered, no confirmation is shown, and the app is forced to exit immediately. The running callback is cut off at the next Lua instruction, then `on_leave` is called. An app cannot intercept the long press.

The back area on a touchscreen is the same as the physical Back key. To go to the previous page, handle `back` and return `true`. On the outermost page return `false`, and after the user confirms they are back in the system.

### Exit confirmation (2.7)

When the `up` of `back` does not return `true`, the host does not end the session at once. It opens the system exit confirmation over the app, so that a mistaken press of Back does not make the app vanish as if it had crashed:

1. The app gets `on_pause` (if a finger is down, a pointer `cancel` is delivered first). While the confirmation is open the app gets no input events, and timers and completion functions are paused as in section 2.
2. The user confirms the exit: the session ends, `on_leave` is called, and the user is back in the system.
3. The user chooses not to exit, or presses Back again in the confirmation: it closes, the app gets `on_resume`, the host redraws one frame, and the app runs on as before.

The host decides the title, text, and buttons of the confirmation; the app cannot change them. Only the “`back` not handled” exit asks for confirmation. These still end the session at once without one: the Back long press forced exit, a script call to `ctx:quit()`, a system key going home (for example the Home long press on `x4_pro`), the lock screen, and power off.

When an app wants to decide how to exit itself (for example its own confirmation with a save reminder, or a game that should leave on a single press), it handles `back` at the outermost level, returns `true`, and calls `ctx:quit()` itself; `ctx:quit()` does not go through the exit confirmation.

This is host behaviour: on a host that implements 2.7, 2.0–2.6 packages also get the exit confirmation without changes. A host at 2.6 or earlier exits immediately when `back` is not handled.

### What produces `back`

| Source | Tap | Long press |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Physical Back key | Delivered as the short press above | Forced exit, as the long press above |
| The Home key below the `x4_pro` screen (a key built into the touchscreen) | Delivered according to system settings, see below | Handled by the system, not delivered |
| Back gesture at the screen edge | Delivered once as a short press | None |

The system first handles the `x4_pro` Home key according to Settings → Buttons → Bottom touch area. Only a tap can reach the app:

| Setting | Options | Default | Effect on the app |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Use button | On, Off in reading, Off | On | With Off, the Home key does nothing. Off in reading only disables it in the reader; in apps it works as usual |
| Tap | No action, Refresh, Back | Back | Only Back delivers `down` and `up` for `back`; with the other two the app receives nothing |
| Double tap | No action, Refresh, Toggle dark, Toggle smoothing, Toggle reading status bar, Toggle light | No action | The system performs the double tap; the app receives nothing. When an action is set, a tap is delivered only after Tap delay (100 ms by default) confirms it is not a double tap |
| Long press | No action, Home, Refresh | Home | Once held for Hold time (500 ms by default, 50–1000 ms), the system performs it and the app receives nothing. With Home the session ends and `on_leave` is called. With No action, pressing counts as a tap |

The 1000 ms long press above does not apply to the Home key: both its duration and its action are system settings that an app cannot intercept.

### Using Back as a function key

An app can use `back` for its own function, for example a Home tap to turn the page, refresh or open and close a menu: do it in `up` and return `true`.

```lua
local menu_open = false

function on_input(ctx, ev)
  if ev.type == "key" and ev.key == "back" then
    if ev.phase ~= "up" then return true end
    if menu_open then
      menu_open = false        -- close the menu first
      ctx:invalidate()
      return true
    end
    return false               -- outermost level: hand over to the system, exits after confirmation
  end
  -- other input...
  return false
end
```

- Return `false` at the outermost level (from 2.7 the host shows the exit confirmation first), or call `ctx:quit()` yourself. The user may set the Home long press to No action, and then `back` is the only way to leave an app on `x4_pro`; an app that always returns `true` and never calls `ctx:quit()` cannot be left.
- The user may change the Home tap to something else or turn the Home key off, and then the app never receives it. Do not make a core function depend only on Back; provide a touch control on screen.
- One tap gives one `down` and one `up`. There is no long press or double tap, and the hold duration is not available.

## Pointer

```lua
{ type = "pointer", phase = "up", x = 0, y = 0, time_ms = 0,
  down_x = 0, down_y = 0, gesture = "tap" }
```

Only one finger is tracked at a time. `x, y` is where this event happened.

| `phase` | When | Extra fields |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `down` | The finger goes down | |
| `move` | It moves while down. At least 4 px from the previous delivery, and at least 50 ms apart; if deliveries cannot keep up, only the latest position is delivered | `down_x` `down_y` |
| `hold` | Held for 700 ms, and both the horizontal and vertical distance from the down point are under 20 px. At most once per press | `down_x` `down_y` |
| `up` | The finger lifts | `down_x` `down_y` `gesture` |
| `cancel` | The system takes over. There is no `up` for this press after that | |

`gesture` on `up` is decided in order. The first match stops the search. Displacement is the `up` point minus the down point:

| Order | gesture | Condition |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `long` | This press delivered a `hold` |
| 2 | `swipe_right` / `swipe_left` | The absolute horizontal displacement is ≥ 50, and it is not smaller than the absolute vertical displacement |
| 3 | `swipe_down` / `swipe_up` | The absolute vertical displacement is ≥ 50, and it is greater than the absolute horizontal displacement |
| 4 | `double_tap` | It would have been a `tap`; the previous `up` was a `tap`; the two downs are at most 300 ms apart, and both the horizontal and vertical distance between the down points are under 20 px |
| 5 | `tap` | Everything else |

The press before a `double_tap` was already delivered as a `tap`. An app that only wants a single tap handles `tap`. Handle `hold` when a long press needs feedback at once.

## Text input

```lua
ctx.input:text({ title = "Search", text = "", max_bytes = 64, secret = false }, function(ctx, text)
  if text then query = text; ctx:invalidate() end
end)
```

After the current callback returns, the host opens the system text-input screen above the app (on a device with touch, the full-page system keyboard, the same keyboard as docked input: it can switch languages and has candidates and a symbol page; with `secret` only the English keyboard is used; when host memory is short it falls back to a simple on-screen keyboard. On a device without touch, key-based character picking). The app receives `on_pause`. After the user confirms or cancels, the app receives `on_resume`, then the completion function is called once as a callback: on confirm, `text` is the string that was entered; on cancel it is nil. Back works as in docked input: it first closes the keyboard list, then clears an unconfirmed composition, and cancels only when there is neither. While the input screen is open, the app receives no input events.

| Field | Rule |
| --- | --- |
| `title` | The caption above the field. Valid UTF-8, at most 64 bytes. May be omitted |
| `text` | Initial content. Valid UTF-8, no longer than `max_bytes`. Defaults to the empty string |
| `max_bytes` | Integer 1–256, default 64. The returned string is no longer than this many bytes |
| `secret` | Boolean. When true the field shows `*`. Default false |

Which characters can be entered is decided by the host input method. At least the printable ASCII range (`0x20`–`0x7E`) is included. The returned string is valid UTF-8. Confirming after the user clears the field yields `""`.

It returns nothing. A value outside the rules returns `nil, "invalid_argument"`. A previous input, (2.1) a dialog, or (2.9) a docked input that has not finished returns `nil, "busy"`. A lock-screen session returns `nil, "inactive"`. An unfinished input is cancelled when the session ends, and the completion function is not called.

## Docked input (2.9)

```lua
local title, ed = "", nil

local function edit_title(ctx)
  ed = ctx.input:edit({
    rect = { x = 32, y = 132, w = 416, h = 40 },   -- text is drawn here; the app draws the border and character count itself
    text = title, placeholder = "What to do", max_chars = 24, enter = "save",
    on_change = function(ctx, text) title = text; ctx:invalidate() end,
    on_end = function(ctx, text, how)
      title, ed = text, nil
      if how == "enter" then save(ctx, title) end
      ctx:invalidate()
    end,
  })
end
```

`ctx.input:edit(opts)` docks the system keyboard at the bottom of the app's picture and edits a piece of text in place. There is no page change: the app does not receive `on_pause`, and timers, networking, and `on_draw` go on as usual. It returns an edit object `ed` (see below).

The bottom `ctx.input.keyboard_h` pixels of the screen belong to the system. From top to bottom they hold the candidate bar and the keyboard, drawn over the app's picture. The app draws the whole screen as usual; the covered part is not visible. The app must lay out the text being edited and the buttons the user needs to tap above `ctx.screen.height - ctx.input.keyboard_h`. `keyboard_h` is an integer and does not change during the session; section 3 gives the value for each profile. On a device without touch it is 0 (see "Without touch").

| Field | Rule |
| --- | --- |
| `rect` | `{ x, y, w, h }` integers. `w` and `h` are at least 1, and the whole block is on the screen. The host draws the text here; see "Text area". May be omitted |
| `text` | Initial content. Valid UTF-8, at most `max_chars` characters. Without `multiline` it may not contain `"\n"`. Default `""` |
| `placeholder` | The hint shown while the text is empty. Valid UTF-8, at most 128 bytes. May be omitted |
| `max_chars` | Integer 1–512, default 128. Characters are counted in Unicode code points, the same as `utf8.len`. Once the limit is reached, further characters are not accepted |
| `kind` | `"text"` (default), `"number"`, `"secret"`, `"letters"`; see below |
| `multiline` | Boolean, default false. When true the text area wraps by character |
| `enter` | The confirm key: `"done"` (default), `"save"`, `"next"`, `"search"`, `"newline"`; see below |
| `on_change` | `function(ctx, text)`, called after the text changes. May be omitted |
| `on_end` | `function(ctx, text, how)`, called once when editing ends. May be omitted |

| `kind` | Keyboard |
| --- | --- |
| `"text"` | The user's current keyboard. Languages can be switched; languages with a dictionary use composition input (Pinyin, Zhuyin, and so on). Has a symbol page |
| `"number"` | Only the symbol page (digits and ASCII punctuation); cannot switch to letters. The host does not check the format |
| `"secret"` | Only the English keyboard, no composition, no candidates, and the user's keyboard settings are not changed. Each character in the text area is drawn as `*` |
| `"letters"` | Only the English keyboard, no composition, no candidates, and the user's keyboard settings are not changed. Has a symbol page. For URLs, accounts, and code |

The confirm key is at the bottom right of the keyboard. By `enter` it shows "Done", "Save", "Next", "Search", or "New line" (written by the host in the system language). Except for `"newline"`, pressing the confirm key ends editing with `how` set to `"enter"`; `"next"` and `"search"` differ only in the label, and the app does the next step in `on_end`. `"newline"` requires `multiline` to be true (otherwise the call returns `nil, "invalid_argument"`); pressing it inserts `"\n"`, and editing can then end only with Back or `ed:close()`. On a device with touch, the `ok` key equals the confirm key.

**Text area**: with `rect`, after the app draws each frame, the host fills `rect` with color 0 and draws in it, with the system body font, the entered text, the cursor, and any unconfirmed composition (underlined). While the text is empty it draws `placeholder`. On a single line, text wider than the box scrolls horizontally; with multiple lines, text taller than the box scrolls vertically; either way the cursor stays inside the box. The app draws the frame, character count, and so on outside `rect`. Without `rect`, the host draws no text in the app's picture; an unconfirmed composition is drawn at the left of the candidate bar, and the app shows the text itself in `on_change` (for example, refreshing search results while typing).

**Callbacks**:

- `on_change(ctx, text)`: called after the committed text changes; `text` is all of the text. An unconfirmed composition does not count. The host may merge several changes in a row into one and pass only the latest text. Any input event the app receives later always arrives after the changes before it have been delivered. When the app requests a redraw in `on_change`, the host presents this frame and the keyboard change together in one presentation.
- `on_end(ctx, text, how)`: called once when editing ends. `text` is the final text; `how` is `"enter"` (confirm key) or `"back"` (Back). Changes not yet delivered do not get their own `on_change`; `on_end` carries them. A new edit can start right away in `on_end`, and the keyboard stays up.

Both are callbacks as described in section 2, with a limit of 1000 ms. Editing ended by `ed:close()` does not call `on_end`. An unfinished edit is cancelled when the session ends, and the callbacks are not called.

**Input while editing**: a pointer, from down to up, belongs entirely to whichever side it went down on.

| Where it goes down | Who gets it |
| --- | --- |
| The bottom `keyboard_h` pixels | The system keyboard; the app does not receive it |
| Inside `rect` | Moves the cursor to the nearest character boundary; the app does not receive it |
| Anywhere else | The app receives the pointer events as usual; the keyboard stays up |

Back first closes an open keyboard list, then clears an unconfirmed composition, and when there is neither it ends editing (`how` is `"back"`); the app does not receive this `back`. While composing, `up` and `down` page through candidates. Other keys go to the app as usual.

While editing, `ctx.input:text`, `ctx.dialog:confirm`, `ctx.dialog:choose`, and another `ctx.input:edit` return `nil, "busy"`. `ctx.dialog:toast` works as usual.

**The edit object**:

```lua
ed:set_text(text)   -- true
local s = ed:text() -- the current text; nil after editing ends
local s = ed:close() -- the final text; nil if already ended
```

- `set_text(text)` replaces all the text, moves the cursor to the end, and drops any unconfirmed composition. The rules are the same as `opts.text`; a value outside them returns `nil, "invalid_argument"`. It does not call `on_change`, and changes not yet delivered are discarded. After editing has ended it returns `nil, "inactive"`.
- `text()` returns the current committed text, which may be newer than the last `on_change` gave. After editing has ended it returns nil.
- `close()` ends editing, hides the keyboard, and returns the final text. It does not call `on_end`. If editing has already ended it returns nil.

**Without touch**: `keyboard_h` is 0, and `ctx.input:edit` instead opens the same full-screen input screen as `ctx.input:text`, limited to 256 bytes. Initial text longer than 256 bytes brings in only the first 256 bytes (without cutting a character); the confirmed text is at most 256 bytes and is then cut to `max_chars`. The app does not receive `on_pause` and keeps running, but its picture is not visible and it receives no input events. After the user confirms, if the text changed, `on_change` is called first, then `on_end` (`how` is `"enter"`). Back cancels and keeps none of this edit's changes; `text` in `on_end` is the text at the start, and `how` is `"back"`. The three methods of `ed` work as usual. The host may also fall back this way when it lacks memory to dock.

It returns `ed`. A value outside the rules returns `nil, "invalid_argument"`. A previous docked input, a `ctx.input:text`, or a dialog that has not finished returns `nil, "busy"`. A lock-screen session returns `nil, "inactive"`.

`ctx.input.edit` is nil on a host of 2.8 or earlier.

## Physical keyboard (2.10)

A Bluetooth keyboard (HID keyboard) that the user connects in system settings works without anything from the app: the arrow keys and Enter act as device keys, and the user types directly while entering text. An app that wants every key (shortcuts, games, terminals) calls `ctx.input:listen({ keyboard = true })`.

While a Bluetooth keyboard is connected, `up`, `down`, `left`, `right`, and `ok` in `ctx.input.keys` are true. Only one Bluetooth input device is connected at a time; a page turner and a keyboard are not connected together.

### When not listening

The keys below are delivered as ordinary `key` events (only `type`, `key`, `phase`, and `time_ms`), one `down`/`up` pair per press. The app receives no other keys.

| Keyboard key | `key` |
| --- | --- |
| ↑ ↓ ← → | `up` `down` `left` `right` |
| PageUp, PageDown | `up`, `down` |
| Enter (including the keypad Enter) | `ok` |
| Esc, Backspace | `back` |

While an arrow key, PageUp, or PageDown is held, the host may deliver several `down`/`up` pairs in a row. A keyboard `back` is handled as a short press of the back key: if `up` is not handled, the exit confirmation appears in the same way. Holding it does not force an exit.

### Typing

While `ctx.input:edit` docked input or `ctx.input:text` (on a device with touch) is open, the keyboard types directly, whether or not the app is listening:

| Key | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| Letters, digits, space, punctuation | Inserted at the cursor, with the US layout. Shift plus a letter types an uppercase letter directly, and CapsLock toggles case. During composition (pinyin and so on), letters go into the composition, and 1–5 pick a candidate on the candidate bar |
| Backspace, Delete | Delete one character before or after the cursor. During composition, delete from the composition first |
| ← → Home End | Move the cursor |
| Enter | During composition, commit the composition; otherwise the same as the confirm key (a line break when `enter = "newline"`) |
| Esc | The same as the back key |
| ↑ ↓ PageUp PageDown | During composition, turn the candidate page |

With `kind = "number"`, letter keys type nothing. Key combinations held with Ctrl, Alt, or Meta, Tab, F1–F12, and ↑ ↓ PageUp PageDown outside composition do not type; they go to the app as usual: as the full events below when listening, or as the ordinary keys in the table above when not listening. A key's `up` goes to the app only if its `down` did.

On a device with no touch, `ctx.input:text` and `ctx.input:edit` falling back to full screen pick characters with keys. The keyboard acts only as the arrow keys, `ok`, and `back`, and cannot type.

### Listening

```lua
function on_enter(ctx)
  ctx.input:listen({ keyboard = true })
end

function on_input(ctx, ev)
  if ev.type == "key" and ev.source == "keyboard" then
    if ev.phase ~= "up" and ev.text then line = line .. ev.text end
    if ev.phase ~= "up" and ev.code == "Backspace" then line = line:sub(1, -2) end
    if ev.mods.ctrl and ev.code == "KeyS" and ev.phase == "down" then save(ctx) end
    ctx:invalidate()
    return true
  end
  return false
end
```

`ctx.input:listen(opts)` chooses whether the app takes the whole keyboard. When `opts.keyboard` is true, every key on the keyboard goes to the app as the event below, and the ordinary keys from "When not listening" above are no longer delivered. When it is false, listening stops. A name that is not written does not change. Every time the app opens, it starts not listening. `listen` can be called in any callback, and also while no keyboard is connected; it takes effect once one connects.

| Field | Rule |
| --- | --- |
| `keyboard` | Boolean. May be omitted |

If `opts` is not a table, or a value is not a boolean, it returns `nil, "invalid_argument"`. A name the host does not know, set to true, also returns `nil, "invalid_argument"` and changes nothing (set to false, it is ignored). On success it returns `true`. 2.10 has only the one name `keyboard`.

The event for each key while listening:

```lua
{ type = "key", source = "keyboard", key = "other", code = "KeyA", text = "a",
  mods = { shift = false, ctrl = false, alt = false, meta = false },
  phase = "down", time_ms = 0 }
```

| Field | Rule |
| --- | --- |
| `source` | `"keyboard"`. Events from device keys and page turners do not have this field |
| `key` | A key with a navigation meaning gives `up` `down` `left` `right` `ok` `back` as in the "When not listening" table, except that Backspace is `"other"`. Every other key is `"other"` |
| `code` | The physical key position, named as in W3C `KeyboardEvent.code`: `KeyA`–`KeyZ`, `Digit0`–`Digit9`, `Enter`, `Escape`, `Backspace`, `Tab`, `Space`, `Minus`, `ArrowUp`, `F1`, `Numpad1`, `ShiftLeft`, `ControlRight`, and so on, independent of layout. A key the host does not know has no such field |
| `text` | The one printable ASCII character (`0x20`–`0x7E`, space is `" "`) this key types with the US layout and Shift. Only on `down` and `repeat`. Absent while Ctrl, Alt, or Meta is held. Not affected by CapsLock |
| `mods` | The modifier keys held at this moment: four booleans `shift`, `ctrl`, `alt`, and `meta`, with no left/right distinction |
| `phase` | `"down"`, `"up"`, or `"repeat"` |
| `time_ms` | The same as for ordinary keys |

- Modifier keys have their own `down` and `up` (`code` is `ShiftLeft` and so on, with no `text`).
- Holding a key produces `repeat`: letters, digits, space, punctuation, Backspace, Delete, arrow keys, PageUp, PageDown, and the keypad character keys start about 450 ms after the press, about every 110 ms, for at most 20 s in a row. Other keys have no `repeat`. An `up` still follows the `repeat` events.
- If the `up` whose `key` is `back` does not return `true`, the host shows the exit confirmation in the same way.
- While typing (see "Typing"), keys taken by the text field are not delivered; the rest are delivered as in the table above.

`ctx.input.listen` is nil on a host of 2.9 or earlier.
entries.example:
ctx.input.keys      -- { up, down, left, right, ok, back }, each a boolean
ctx.input.pointer   -- true when there is a touchscreen

entries.content:
# 5. Presenting a frame

```lua
ctx:invalidate()
ctx:invalidate("full")
ctx:defer_full_refresh(ms)
ctx.perf:info()
```

`invalidate` asks for one frame to be drawn and presented after the current callback returns. It returns nothing. Called from `on_draw`, it is queued for the next frame, and the waveform counts toward that next frame (a lock-screen session is the exception; see section 15). The argument is the waveform: omitted means a partial refresh; `"full"` is a full refresh, which clears ghosting and flashes once. If one frame is requested more than once, a single `"full"` makes the whole frame a full refresh. Any other argument returns `nil, "invalid_argument"`. (2.11) When a `g:image` call in the frame sets `gray = true`, the frame is a full refresh with the grayscale waveform; see "Gray frames" in section 3. The argument of `invalidate` does not choose that waveform.

Every so many partial refreshes, the system inserts a full refresh on its own. The count is the one the user picked in system settings (often 6 to 30; Gancao firmware defaults to 30, so after 29 partial refreshes the 30th frame is a full refresh). A full refresh takes much longer than a partial one (about 1.5 seconds on the Gancao X4 Pro / X4 Classic, against about 0.65 seconds), so a continuous animation shows a pause there. `defer_full_refresh(ms)` makes presentations during the next `ms` milliseconds neither trigger nor count toward that automatic full refresh. Use it while paging or dragging so the screen does not flash. `ms` is an integer from 1 to 60000. It returns nothing. A later call replaces the deadline. `invalidate("full")` is not affected.

One frame accepts at most 1024 drawing commands. Each line `g:text_box` draws counts as one. The call that would exceed the limit returns `nil, "limit_exceeded"` and is not added to this frame. Commands already accepted stay.

`ctx.perf:info()` returns a table. Every field is an integer greater than or equal to 0. A field for something that has not happened yet is 0:

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `tick_us` | Microseconds of the latest `on_tick` |
| `draw_us` | Microseconds of the latest `on_draw` |
| `cmd_count` | Commands accepted by the latest frame |
| `image_count` | How many times `g:image` ran in the latest frame |
| `asset_hit` `asset_miss` | Image-cache hits and misses, accumulated for the session |
| `draw_frame` | Frames completed |

## How long a frame takes

`invalidate` takes no region. Gancao firmware presents every frame as a whole-screen partial refresh, and the time it takes has almost nothing to do with how many pixels the frame changed: about 650 ms on the X4 Pro (section 2), so changing one digit takes as long as replacing the whole screen. A frame requested while a presentation is in progress does not queue; it is merged into the next frame (section 2), so calling `invalidate` more often is neither faster nor does it pile up.

A frame's time has three parts: the script's `on_draw`, the host turning this frame's commands into pixels, and the presentation. `draw_us` counts only the first part: when `on_draw` returns, the pixels are not drawn yet, let alone presented. The second part is not in `perf`; estimate it with the table in the next subsection. The Gancao X4 Pro starts drawing the next frame before the previous fast refresh ends, timed by how long the previous frame took to draw (not for a full refresh, nor right after power-on before the refresh time has been measured), so while the first two parts together stay within about 0.5 seconds, the frame interval is the refresh time; anything beyond that is added to every frame.

## Making smooth animations and games

This subsection is advice, not a requirement. The times in the table were measured on the Gancao X4 Pro drawing the full 480×800 screen; smaller drawing scales roughly with area. Other devices are faster or slower, but which ways of drawing are fast and which are slow stays the same.

| Way of drawing | Full-screen time |
| --- | --- |
| `g:clear`, solid `g:rect` fills | 1–2 ms |
| Off-screen layer drawn back at its own size (no `w`, `h`, or the layer's own size), not rotated, not flipped, no `radius` | about 8 ms |
| 1-bit image drawn at its own size under the same conditions; `color`, `invert`, `background`, and 1-bit transparency make no difference (with 4-bit or 8-bit transparency, use the next row) | about 20 ms |
| Any other image drawing: scaling, flipping, rotation, `radius`, 4-level or 16-level images | 350–450 ms |

- **Advance by time.** Move continuously by "speed × `dt_ms`" (section 2). Two frames are about 0.65 seconds apart; when a step would jump too far, switch to moving by cells or steps.
- **Request a frame only when the picture changed.** Every `invalidate` is a whole-screen partial refresh: it costs power and speeds up ghosting. When idle, `set_tick(0)`; for a clock face, use `ctx:after` to aim at the next minute; requests in the same callback count as one frame.
- **`on_draw` only draws.** Work out movement, collisions, and pathfinding in `on_tick` and keep them in state; `on_draw` just draws from state, and the shorter the better. Do saving, networking, and heavy computation in other callbacks, split into pieces of a few tens of milliseconds (continue with `ctx:after`): callbacks run one after another, and one long piece delays the start of drawing the next frame.
- **Make art pure black and white, exported at display size.** The packager produces a 1-bit image only when every visible pixel is pure black or pure white (appendix A); grey anti-aliased edges turn the whole image into 16 levels. Turn anti-aliasing off when exporting PNG, and dither photos to pure black and white first. Export one image per size you need, and one facing left and one facing right; do not scale or `flip_x` every frame.
- **Draw what does not move into a layer.** Content that rarely changes, such as backgrounds, maps, and boards, is drawn with `layer:draw` in `on_load` or when it changes; each frame draws it back with `g:image(layer, 0, 0)` and then draws the small moving things. Content that needs scaling, flipping, rotation, or a lot of text can also be drawn into a layer first, so each frame pays only for drawing it back. At most 4 layers (section 11).
- **Defer the automatic full refresh during continuous motion.** Call `ctx:defer_full_refresh(ms)` while moving so the screen does not flash and stop for 1.5 seconds midway; when movement stops or the page changes, `invalidate("full")` to clear ghosting.
- **Keep a state visible for at least one frame.** A state shorter than one frame interval (a blink, a pressed highlight) may miss every frame; to be seen it must last until the next frame has finished, for example restore a pressed highlight with `ctx:after(700, ...)`.
entries.example:
ctx:invalidate()
ctx:invalidate("full")
ctx:defer_full_refresh(ms)
ctx.perf:info()
